meta.label: News sources
meta.attribution: Scored on funding and structure - the things that shape independence from advertiser and owner pressure - NOT on political viewpoint. Curated from public ownership records, funding disclosures, editorial standards, and press-accountability sources. Read widely and across perspectives. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare news sources by editorial independence, disclosure, nonprofit structure, and depth.

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Associated Press
products.description: A not-for-profit wire cooperative whose reporting underpins many local and national news outlets.

independence.note: AP describes itself as an independent news cooperative beholden to facts and public interest.

transparency.note: AP publishes news values and correction practices for accuracy, bias, and errors.

nonprofit.note: AP says it is a not-for-profit cooperative that reinvests revenue into news production.

depth.note: AP says its journalists work in nearly 100 countries and all 50 U.S. states, with teams in 230 locations.

accessibility.note: AP News is free to read for many current stories and is widely syndicated through member outlets.

products.name: Reuters
products.description: A global commercial wire service with formal trust principles and broad original reporting capacity.

independence.note: Reuters is for-profit but bound by Trust Principles requiring integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

transparency.note: Reuters standards include open correction of errors, balance, freedom from bias, and conflict disclosure.

nonprofit.note: Reuters is a commercial news agency, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: Reuters describes a large international reporting operation across countries, languages, text, photo, and video.

accessibility.note: Reuters.com offers some direct reading with registration/metering alongside syndication to other outlets.

products.name: ProPublica
products.description: A nonprofit investigative newsroom focused on abuses of power, with free republication and donor funding.

independence.note: ProPublica is a nonprofit investigative newsroom funded by donations rather than a proprietor or shareholders.

transparency.note: ProPublica publishes public reports three times a year plus annual financial statements and Form 990 filings.

nonprofit.note: ProPublica identifies as a nonprofit newsroom focused on investigative journalism.

depth.note: ProPublica says it reports in all 50 states, partners with local newsrooms, and focuses on investigative public-interest work.

accessibility.note: ProPublica permits broad free republication of many stories under stated rules.

products.name: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists
products.description: A donor-funded global investigative network built for cross-border accountability projects.

independence.note: ICIJ is an independent global network of investigative journalists collaborating across borders.

transparency.note: ICIJ publishes corporate documents and information about its nonprofit status.

nonprofit.note: ICIJ states it is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit headquartered in Washington, DC.

depth.note: ICIJ's model is built around large collaborative investigations with hundreds of journalists in many countries.

accessibility.note: ICIJ publishes investigation pages freely online with partner distribution.

products.name: The Marshall Project
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom focused on criminal justice, immigration enforcement, prisons, and accountability reporting.

independence.note: The Marshall Project describes itself as nonprofit journalism about criminal justice.

transparency.note: Its code of ethics commits to accuracy, fairness, independence, and prominent corrections.

nonprofit.note: The Marshall Project identifies as a nonprofit news organization.

depth.note: The newsroom's mission page centers accountability journalism on the U.S. criminal justice system and links to local and impact work.

accessibility.note: Its reporting is published free online with newsletters and local partnerships.

products.name: The Markup
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom that investigates technology, data, and algorithmic power with method-driven reporting.

independence.note: The Markup describes itself as a nonprofit newsroom challenging technology to serve the public good.

transparency.note: Its public-interest tech investigations commonly publish methods, data, and tools alongside reporting.

nonprofit.note: The Markup identifies as a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: Its editorial focus is technology accountability and data-driven investigations.

accessibility.note: The Markup publishes its journalism freely online.

products.name: Rest of World
products.description: A nonprofit publication covering technology's impact outside the usual US/Western Europe center of gravity.

independence.note: Rest of World says it independently reports on technology's impact outside the West without a paywall.

transparency.note: It publishes supporter information and funding disclosures.

nonprofit.note: Rest of World identifies as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit publication.

depth.note: The publication focuses on on-the-ground reporting about technology outside Silicon Valley and Western Europe.

accessibility.note: Rest of World says its reporting is available without a paywall.

products.name: Inside Climate News
products.description: A nonprofit, nonpartisan climate newsroom focused on investigations, accountability, misinformation, and environmental justice.

independence.note: Inside Climate News describes itself as nonprofit, nonpartisan, and focused on watchdog reporting around climate and energy.

transparency.note: Its donor-transparency page identifies governance, nonprofit status, donor categories, and a commitment to factual, fair, fearless journalism.

nonprofit.note: Inside Climate News says it is an independent not-for-profit approved by the IRS as a 501(c)(3) public charity.

depth.note: Its stated mission centers essential reporting, investigation, and analysis on climate, misinformation, polluters, environmental justice and solutions.

accessibility.note: Inside Climate News publishes climate coverage online without a paywall and relies on reader donations.

products.name: NPR
products.description: A US public-media network producing radio, podcast, local-station, and web journalism; its local ecosystem is under new funding pressure.

independence.note: NPR is a member-supported public media network with mixed public, station, sponsorship, and donor funding.

transparency.note: NPR maintains a public editor and public-facing ethics/accountability material.

nonprofit.note: NPR operates as nonprofit public media rather than a shareholder-owned news company.

depth.note: NPR produces original national, international, audio, and explanatory reporting through a public-radio network.

accessibility.note: NPR remains free online and via stations, but CPB's 2025 defunding put local public-media access and station capacity under pressure.

products.name: PBS NewsHour
products.description: A public-media news program and newsroom centered on broadcast and video public-affairs reporting, now in a stressed local-station ecosystem.

independence.note: PBS is public media with editorial standards intended to protect journalistic integrity.

transparency.note: PBS publishes editorial standards and funding standards for editorial integrity.

nonprofit.note: PBS NewsHour is part of the public-media system rather than a commercial shareholder newsroom.

depth.note: PBS NewsHour is a long-form public-affairs program and newsroom.

accessibility.note: PBS NewsHour remains free online and on broadcast, but CPB's wind-down after federal funding loss weakens local public-media distribution capacity.

products.name: Democracy Now!
products.description: A daily independent nonprofit news hour with free broadcast, web, audio, video, and transcript access.

independence.note: Democracy Now says it does not accept advertising, underwriting, or government-agency funding and relies on viewer/listener contributions.

transparency.note: It publishes about/contact information and funding model statements, though less granular donor reporting than some nonprofit peers.

nonprofit.note: Democracy Now identifies as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit news organization.

depth.note: The outlet produces a daily global news hour with headlines and in-depth interviews on major public issues.

accessibility.note: Programs, web stories, podcasts, video, audio, and transcripts are published freely online.

products.name: BBC News
products.description: A large public-service broadcaster with global reach and charter-backed editorial standards.

independence.note: The BBC editorial standards cite charter-backed independence, editorial freedom, and licence-fee safeguards.

transparency.note: BBC standards describe accountability, complaints handling, published findings, and corrections/apologies.

nonprofit.note: BBC is a public corporation with a public-service mission, not a commercial proprietor newsroom.

depth.note: The BBC maintains a large global newsroom and public-service news remit.

accessibility.note: BBC News is free online in many markets, with broad public-service distribution.

products.name: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism
products.description: A UK nonprofit investigative newsroom that works with publishing partners on public-interest investigations.

independence.note: The Bureau is a nonprofit investigative newsroom supported by foundations, individuals, and partners.

transparency.note: It publishes its funding approach and donor/funding basis.

nonprofit.note: The Bureau describes itself as a nonprofit investigative newsroom.

depth.note: Its stated purpose is public-interest investigative journalism, often with partner publication.

accessibility.note: The Bureau publishes investigations freely online and through media partners.

products.name: The Guardian
products.description: A trust-owned international newsroom with broad free access and reader-funded reporting.

independence.note: The Guardian is owned by the Scott Trust, which reinvests profits and has no proprietor dividend.

transparency.note: The Guardian publishes a detailed editorial code, corrections channel, complaints process and annual financial reporting.

nonprofit.note: The Guardian is trust-owned and profit-seeking/reinvesting, not a conventional nonprofit charity.

depth.note: Guardian Media Group reports growing global revenue and continued strategic investment in journalism, technology and global expansion.

accessibility.note: The Guardian describes its journalism as freely available to all and supported by more than 1.3 million recurring digital supporters.

products.name: The New York Times
products.description: A major subscription-funded national and international newsroom with deep reporting capacity, public-company economics, and family-trust control.

independence.note: The 2025 Form 10-K says the Ochs-Sulzberger family trust holds about 95% of Class B stock and can elect 70% of the board.

transparency.note: The Times publishes an Ethical Journalism handbook and integrity guidelines for newsroom and opinion work.

nonprofit.note: The 2025 Form 10-K presents The New York Times Company as a subscription- and advertising-funded public media company, not a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: The 2025 Form 10-K describes a large news product plus Athletic, Audio, Cooking, Games, Wirecutter, licensing and print businesses.

accessibility.note: The 2025 Form 10-K describes a subscription-led model across digital, bundle, standalone and print products, so full access is paywalled.

products.name: CalMatters
products.description: A nonprofit, nonpartisan newsroom devoted to California policy, politics, explainers, and accountability reporting.

independence.note: CalMatters describes itself as a nonpartisan, nonprofit newsroom covering California public life.

transparency.note: CalMatters publishes funding sources, policies, and federal tax ID information.

nonprofit.note: CalMatters identifies as a nonprofit news organization.

depth.note: It specializes in California policy, politics, explainers, and accountability reporting.

accessibility.note: CalMatters publishes its journalism free online and supports republishing/newsletter access.

products.name: The Texas Tribune
products.description: A nonprofit, nonpartisan Texas newsroom focused on state politics, policy, public data, explainers, and local expansion.

independence.note: The Tribune says editorial decisions are made by journalists alone and not influenced by donors.

transparency.note: It publishes funders, policies and Trust Project transparency commitments, including corrections and source disclosure norms.

nonprofit.note: The Texas Tribune identifies as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

depth.note: Its beat is Texas politics, public policy, state government, data, events and accountability journalism.

accessibility.note: The Tribune publishes its journalism freely online and supports newsletters, events, republishing and public-service distribution.

products.name: KFF Health News
products.description: A national health-policy newsroom useful for health care, insurance, public health, Medicare, Medicaid and health-cost reporting.

independence.note: KFF describes itself as an independent source for health policy research, polling and journalism.

transparency.note: KFF Health News explains outside funding rules and says it accepts support only from sources that do not compromise independence or mission.

nonprofit.note: KFF Health News is one of KFF's core operating programs, and KFF is a nonprofit health-policy organization.

depth.note: The newsroom produces in-depth journalism about health issues, backed by KFF's health policy research context.

accessibility.note: KFF Health News lets other outlets republish staff stories and many photos free of charge under a Creative Commons license.

products.name: The Hechinger Report
products.description: A specialist education newsroom focused on inequality, innovation and accountability from early childhood through college and careers.

independence.note: Hechinger says diverse funding from individuals and organizations with a range of views supports editorial independence.

transparency.note: It publishes an editorial-independence policy and explains its funding safeguards.

nonprofit.note: The Hechinger Report identifies as a nonprofit newsroom covering education inequality and innovation.

depth.note: Its mission page says it covers education from the earliest years through college and careers, with emphasis on inequality and innovation.

accessibility.note: Hechinger says its nonprofit in-depth independent journalism is provided free to readers.

products.name: THE CITY
products.description: A New York City nonprofit newsroom focused on civic accountability, local services, neighborhoods and public power.

independence.note: Cause IQ describes City Report as an independent nonprofit newsroom built around the public value of local news.

transparency.note: Its public donation page identifies THE CITY as local nonprofit news and gives readers a direct support route.

nonprofit.note: City Report is listed as the nonprofit organization behind THE CITY.

depth.note: Cause IQ summarizes its work as investigative journalism, explanatory reporting and consistent ground-up coverage of important NYC issues.

accessibility.note: THE CITY publishes free local coverage and asks readers for donations rather than relying on a hard paywall.

products.name: LAist
products.description: A Southern California nonprofit newsroom and public-radio home for local explainers, accountability, service journalism and community reporting.

independence.note: LAist describes itself as an audience-funded nonprofit news organization.

transparency.note: LAist publishes editorial ethics guidelines and correction standards for its newsroom.

nonprofit.note: LAist says it is an audience-funded nonprofit news organization and home of LAist.com and LAist 89.3 FM.

depth.note: Its about page says the newsroom helps people make sense of Southern California through useful, community-connected reporting.

accessibility.note: LAist publishes free local news online and through public radio, funded by audience support.

products.name: Gothamist
products.description: A New York City local-news site powered by WNYC/New York Public Radio, useful for civic, neighborhood, transit and daily-life coverage.

independence.note: Gothamist is presented as a nonprofit newsroom powered by WNYC and brought to readers by New York Public Radio.

transparency.note: Gothamist publishes staff, contact and feedback channels, though its policy detail is less extensive than some nonprofit peers.

nonprofit.note: The site labels itself a nonprofit newsroom and is part of New York Public Radio.

depth.note: Its homepage and sections cover NYC news, arts, events, food and local accountability reporting.

accessibility.note: Gothamist publishes local coverage freely online and asks readers to donate.

products.name: VTDigger
products.description: A statewide Vermont nonprofit newsroom with a strong model for local accountability, government, climate and community reporting.

independence.note: VTDigger identifies itself as an independent nonprofit journalism organization serving Vermont communities.

transparency.note: Its annual report describes impact, operations and reader-supported nonprofit journalism.

nonprofit.note: VTDigger states in its FAQ that it is a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: The annual report frames VTDigger's work around helping Vermonters understand communities, government and statewide issues.

accessibility.note: VTDigger publishes its reporting online with reader support rather than a hard subscription-only model.

products.name: MinnPost
products.description: A Minnesota nonprofit newsroom focused on state government, metro issues, health, environment, arts and civic life.

independence.note: MinnPost says it is an independent nonprofit newsroom with no political or commercial interest.

transparency.note: Its about page links financial reports, donor lists, staff, board and ethics information.

nonprofit.note: MinnPost identifies itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: MinnPost says it produces in-depth reporting on consequential civic and cultural affairs in Minnesota.

accessibility.note: MinnPost says all reporting is free, with no paywalls, and original reporting can be republished by partners.

products.name: Wisconsin Watch
products.description: A Wisconsin investigative nonprofit focused on government integrity, quality of life and statewide accountability reporting.

independence.note: Wisconsin Watch says funders have no influence over editorial decisions and that it does not accept anonymous donations.

transparency.note: Its funding page publicly lists donor and funding transparency by year.

nonprofit.note: Wisconsin Watch is a project of the Wisconsin Center for Investigative Journalism, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

depth.note: The Trust Project identifies Wisconsin Watch as focused on government integrity and quality-of-life issues.

accessibility.note: Wisconsin Watch publishes public-interest reporting online with reader membership support.

products.name: Investigate Midwest
products.description: A nonprofit watchdog newsroom covering agriculture, water, labor, rural life and environmental issues across the Midwest.

independence.note: Investigate Midwest describes itself as an independent nonprofit newsroom.

transparency.note: It publishes support, FAQ-style and donor pages, though policy detail is less visible than the strongest nonprofit peers.

nonprofit.note: Report for America identifies the Midwest Center for Investigative Reporting as a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: Its reporting centers agriculture, water, labor and environmental issues affecting rural and Midwestern communities.

accessibility.note: Investigate Midwest publishes its watchdog reporting online and asks readers for support.

products.name: Capital B
products.description: A Black-led nonprofit local and national newsroom reporting for Black communities, with national coverage and local desks.

independence.note: Capital B says it does not accept money at the expense of editorial independence.

transparency.note: Its about page explains its philanthropic, membership and underwriting funding mix.

nonprofit.note: Capital B identifies as a Black-led nonprofit local and national news organization.

depth.note: The American Journalism Project describes Capital B as building nonprofit newsrooms for Black communities across the country.

accessibility.note: Capital B publishes free local and national reporting and invites reader support.

products.name: High Country News
products.description: A reader-supported nonprofit newsroom covering the US West, public lands, Indigenous affairs, climate, water and rural power.

independence.note: High Country News says it is independent and reader-supported, with readers supplying most operating revenue.

transparency.note: Its support FAQ gives a revenue breakdown across reader support, grants and advertising.

nonprofit.note: High Country News presents itself as a nonprofit independent magazine.

depth.note: Its about page describes more than 50 years of reporting on the complexities of the West.

accessibility.note: Reader support funds much of the journalism, but the magazine model includes subscription and donation asks rather than universal public access.

products.name: Prism
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom led by journalists of color, focused on workers' rights, racial justice, disability justice, health, environment, gender and LGBTQIA+ issues.

independence.note: MacArthur describes Prism as a national nonprofit newsroom producing in-depth journalism on justice-focused beats.

transparency.note: Public third-party profiles describe Prism's nonprofit structure, though donor and policy detail is less findable than leading transparency peers.

nonprofit.note: GuideStar lists Prism Reports Inc. as a nonprofit profile.

depth.note: MacArthur says Prism produces explanatory, accountability and investigative reporting centered on impacted communities.

accessibility.note: Prism's public site publishes reporting online, with access supported by nonprofit and philanthropic funding.

products.name: The Conversation
products.description: An academic-news nonprofit pairing subject-matter experts with editors for explanatory journalism.

independence.note: The Conversation's model pairs academic authors with journalist editors rather than a proprietor news agenda.

transparency.note: Authors disclose expertise, institution, funding, and conflicts on article pages.

nonprofit.note: The Conversation is structured as a nonprofit/charity network across regional editions.

depth.note: Its niche is expert explanatory journalism written by academics and edited by journalists.

accessibility.note: The Conversation publishes free articles and republishing guidance under Creative Commons terms.

products.name: The Christian Science Monitor
products.description: A mission-driven international newsroom known for constructive, global coverage with subscription limits.

independence.note: The Monitor describes itself as an international news organization with a distinct global, constructive mission.

transparency.note: The Monitor publishes about, terms, and contributor/editorial materials, though less granular than some nonprofit peers.

nonprofit.note: The Monitor is mission-driven and supported partly through an operating fund, but its church ownership requires context.

depth.note: The Monitor emphasizes thoughtful global coverage and analysis rather than high-volume breaking news.

accessibility.note: The Monitor offers some free access with subscriptions/metering for fuller access.

products.name: Wikipedia / Wikinews
products.description: A nonprofit reference commons that summarizes sourced reporting rather than producing original news.

independence.note: Wikipedia is hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation, a nonprofit that does not use advertising revenue.

transparency.note: The Wikimedia Foundation describes Wikipedia's open edit histories, talk pages, consensus process and transparency reports.

nonprofit.note: The Wikimedia Foundation says it is the nonprofit behind Wikipedia.

depth.note: Harvard's source guide frames Wikipedia as useful background, but advises following citations for serious research, so depth varies by topic.

accessibility.note: Wikipedia is free, multilingual, and ad-free.

products.name: Ground News
products.description: A bias-comparison tool that shows how different outlets cover a story, not an original newsroom.

independence.note: Ground News is an independent comparison platform, not a newsroom or publisher.

transparency.note: Ground News explains that bias ratings average independent monitoring organizations and their methods.

nonprofit.note: Ground News is a commercial subscription/freemium tool rather than a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: It aggregates and compares source coverage; it does not primarily produce original reporting.

accessibility.note: Ground News has a free layer plus paid features for deeper comparison tools.

products.name: AllSides
products.description: A media-bias rating and comparison service for checking coverage across ideological perspectives.

independence.note: AllSides publishes ownership information and says ownership spans people across the political spectrum.

transparency.note: AllSides publishes its media-bias rating methods, including editorial reviews and blind bias surveys.

nonprofit.note: AllSides is a for-profit / mission-driven company rather than a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: It rates, aggregates, and compares coverage rather than doing original beat reporting.

accessibility.note: AllSides offers many bias ratings and comparison pages free online.

products.name: Financial Times
products.description: A global business and economics newsroom with unusually strong editorial standards and a subscription-heavy access model.

independence.note: FT Group is part of Nikkei Inc., so the independence score balances corporate ownership with stated editorial safeguards.

transparency.note: The FT publishes an editorial code that is mandatory for editorial staff and explains its self-regulation regime.

nonprofit.note: FT Group is a commercial business-information and news group, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: FT positions the Financial Times and FT Specialist as business-information, news and services operations with deep professional coverage.

accessibility.note: Standard and Premium Digital subscriptions gate full FT journalism, making access materially less open than free newsrooms.

products.name: The Economist
products.description: A subscription-led global weekly with a distinctive editorial line and governance designed around editorial independence.

independence.note: The Economist says its independence is protected by editorial culture and a special ownership/governance structure.

transparency.note: The Economist publishes reader-facing FAQ material including correction practices and account/subscription policies.

nonprofit.note: The Economist Group reports revenue, operating profit and dividends, so it is not a nonprofit news organization.

depth.note: The Economist Group reports 1.29 million subscriptions and a large weekly global journalism operation.

accessibility.note: The main product is sold as unlimited-access paid subscriptions, with discounts but not broad free access.

products.name: Axios
products.description: A concise digital newsroom and newsletter network with free consumer coverage plus paid professional products.

independence.note: Cox Enterprises acquired Axios in 2022, making family-owned corporate media ownership the relevant independence context.

transparency.note: Axios publishes a mission page and an editorial ethics policy covering truth, verification and conflicts.

nonprofit.note: Axios is a commercial media company owned by Cox Enterprises, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Axios publishes national, local, newsletter and professional news products; its format emphasizes concise reporting over long-form depth.

accessibility.note: Many Axios newsletters are free, while deeper vertical products such as Axios Pro are paid.

products.name: Vox
products.description: An explanatory news site with strong public methods pages, broad free access, and 2026 ownership transition context.

independence.note: Vox Media announced Vox would move into a new Lupa-owned media company, so private ownership is material context.

transparency.note: Vox publishes funding and ethics pages explaining advertising, grants, membership support, conflicts and sponsored-content labeling.

nonprofit.note: Vox is a commercial media property, despite some grant-supported journalism, not a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: Vox's stated mission is to help people understand a complicated world through explainers, podcasts and general-interest coverage.

accessibility.note: Vox makes much of its journalism free online while asking for membership support.

products.name: USA Today
products.description: A mass-market national news brand at the center of a large US local-to-national publishing network.

independence.note: USA TODAY Co. is a publicly traded media company, so corporate chain ownership shapes the independence score.

transparency.note: USA TODAY Network publishes principles of ethical conduct for newsrooms across platforms.

nonprofit.note: USA TODAY Co. is a commercial publishing and digital media company, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: USA TODAY Network describes itself as the largest local-to-national publishing and digital media organization in the country.

accessibility.note: USA Today mixes free access with subscriber-only unlimited access, eNewspaper and member benefits.

products.name: The Hill
products.description: A high-reach US politics and policy outlet with free access and Nexstar corporate ownership.

independence.note: Nexstar acquired The Hill in 2021, making commercial broadcaster ownership central to the independence score.

transparency.note: The Hill discloses its advertising audience and business positioning, but exposes fewer detailed public newsroom standards than top-scoring outlets.

nonprofit.note: The Hill is a Nexstar commercial media property, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Nexstar described The Hill as a political digital media platform with more than 100 journalists covering political news and events.

accessibility.note: The Hill is primarily advertising-supported and publishes substantial politics coverage free online.

products.name: Daily Mail / MailOnline
products.description: A huge free-to-read UK-originated tabloid and online news operation with strong reach but weaker public-interest structure signals.

independence.note: Daily Mail is part of dmg media, a large commercial media group, so corporate/private publisher ownership weighs on independence.

transparency.note: MailOnline's readers-editor page says UK journalists follow the Editors' Code and the publisher is an IPSO member.

nonprofit.note: dmg media is a commercial publisher, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: dmg media emphasizes breaking news, exclusives, commentary and mass-market verticals rather than a public-interest investigative model.

accessibility.note: dmg media describes Daily Mail as a global, high-reach digital news brand, and MailOnline is broadly free to read.

products.name: Newsmax
products.description: A commercially owned cable and digital news outlet with wide free reach and serious trust flags from election-defamation litigation.

independence.note: Newsmax investor materials describe a publicly held media company headed by founder and CEO Christopher Ruddy.

transparency.note: Newsmax has investor filings, but public editorial-standards visibility is weak and 2025 defamation settlements are material trust context.

nonprofit.note: Newsmax is a commercial media company with investor relations and public filings, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Newsmax operates cable, streaming, app, web and magazine properties, but its public-interest depth score is limited by trust and standards concerns.

accessibility.note: Newsmax says its properties include cable, free streaming, app, website and magazine distribution reaching more than 40 million Americans regularly.

products.name: Google News
products.description: A highly accessible algorithmic news gateway that ranks and personalizes other publishers rather than producing journalism itself.

independence.note: Google News is a Google platform, so the main independence issue is platform power over publisher visibility rather than newsroom ownership.

transparency.note: Google explains broad news-ranking and publisher-transparency signals, while detailed ranking weight remains algorithmic and opaque.

nonprofit.note: Google News is a commercial Google product, not a nonprofit, public-media or reader-owned news source.

depth.note: Google News sends users to publisher content and is not itself an original reporting newsroom.

accessibility.note: Google News is free and highly available, though linked articles may lead to publisher paywalls.

products.name: Apple News
products.description: A device-tied news platform and subscription bundle that curates and distributes publisher journalism rather than operating as a newsroom.

independence.note: Apple News is an Apple platform and subscription product, so platform control and bundle economics shape the independence score.

transparency.note: Apple publishes product and publisher documentation, but users get limited visibility into ranking and curation decisions.

nonprofit.note: Apple News+ is a commercial Apple subscription bundle, not a nonprofit or public-media newsroom.

depth.note: Apple News aggregates and distributes publisher articles; original reporting depth depends on included publications.

accessibility.note: Apple News+ requires compatible Apple devices and a paid subscription for its full publication bundle.

products.name: Al Jazeera English
products.description: A state-funded international newsroom with strong global coverage and material Qatar ownership context.

independence.note: State Media Monitor classifies AJMN as state-controlled, citing state-linked governance, funding dependence and constrained Qatari domestic coverage.

transparency.note: Al Jazeera publishes a code of ethics, but State Media Monitor notes undisclosed finances and no statutory guarantee of editorial independence.

nonprofit.note: State Media Monitor describes AJMN as a private corporation for public benefit, funded partly by Qatar rather than by ordinary shareholders.

depth.note: State Media Monitor reports more than 70 bureaus, 3,000+ staff, 150+ countries and 430 million-home reach.

accessibility.note: Al Jazeera English publishes news freely online.

products.name: Bloomberg
products.description: A privately owned financial-news and data company with deep business reporting and premium paywalls.

independence.note: Forbes reports Michael Bloomberg owns 88% of Bloomberg LP, making founder ownership a material independence context.

transparency.note: Bloomberg Live guidelines say events must follow Bloomberg News editorial standards and preserve editorial independence, but ownership/funding disclosure is limited.

nonprofit.note: Bloomberg Media describes Bloomberg as a business and financial information, news and insight company, not a nonprofit news organization.

depth.note: Bloomberg Media says it has 3,000+ news professionals and analysts and 120+ global news bureaus.

accessibility.note: Bloomberg's consumer site and premium business products make much of its deepest reporting less accessible than free public-interest outlets.

products.name: The Washington Post
products.description: A major national newsroom with deep accountability reporting and public standards, balanced by billionaire ownership and subscription access.

independence.note: The Post says it is owned by Jeff Bezos, making single-owner billionaire control a material independence context.

transparency.note: The Post help center points readers to its policies portal for mission, ethics, verification, diversity, ownership, corrections, sources and reader engagement.

nonprofit.note: The Washington Post is a private for-profit newspaper rather than a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: The Post's policies portal includes verification, fact-checking, source, corrections and reader-engagement standards, supporting a high depth score.

accessibility.note: Full access is subscription-based, including standard and premium digital packages.

products.name: The Wall Street Journal
products.description: A deeply resourced business and finance newsroom with strong standards and a hard subscription model under News Corp/Dow Jones ownership.

independence.note: The Journal is published by Dow Jones, a News Corp business, so corporate media ownership is central to the independence score.

transparency.note: WSJ says its journalists follow rigorous fairness and integrity standards, and Dow Jones publishes a code of conduct.

nonprofit.note: Dow Jones and WSJ are commercial News Corp businesses, not nonprofit or public-media news organizations.

depth.note: WSJ's own positioning centers business, financial, market, policy and world news coverage, with large subscriber-supported reporting capacity.

accessibility.note: Most full WSJ access requires a paid digital or print subscription, with some institutional/student routes.

products.name: CNN
products.description: A huge commercial TV and digital newsroom with global reach, strong accessibility, and corporate-media ownership limits.

independence.note: CNN's fact sheet says CNN is a division of Warner Bros. Discovery, so it is a corporate media outlet rather than an independent nonprofit.

transparency.note: CNN publishes fact sheets and journalism training materials, but its full internal editorial standards are less publicly inspectable than some print peers.

nonprofit.note: CNN is a commercial Warner Bros. Discovery division, not a nonprofit, public, or reader-owned newsroom.

depth.note: CNN's fact sheet lists 37 bureaus worldwide, supporting broad original reporting capacity.

accessibility.note: CNN publishes a large amount of free web news, while live TV and premium access are tied to pay-TV or subscription products.

products.name: Fox News
products.description: A dominant US cable-news brand that is extremely accessible, but commercially owned and less transparent than higher-scoring public-interest newsrooms.

independence.note: Fox News says it is owned by Fox Corporation, making large commercial media ownership the core independence context.

transparency.note: Fox Corporation publishes broad guiding principles, but Fox News exposes less detailed newsroom standards than the most transparent outlets here.

nonprofit.note: Fox News is a Fox Corporation commercial brand, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: Fox News has national cable, digital and video operations with large reach, but the public depth signal is weaker than investigative or wire-service peers.

accessibility.note: FoxNews.com is broadly free to read, while full live cable viewing depends on cable, streaming, or pay-TV access.

products.name: Politico
products.description: A policy-heavy political newsroom with useful free coverage and deep Pro products, now under Axel Springer ownership.

independence.note: Axel Springer says it became 100% owner of Politico and related properties in 2021, replacing founder ownership with publisher ownership.

transparency.note: Politico publicly explains its advertising, sponsorship and Pro subscription model when responding to funding claims.

nonprofit.note: Axel Springer lists POLITICO among its media brands and says it became 100% owner in 2021, so this is commercial publisher ownership rather than nonprofit/public media.

depth.note: Politico Pro positions itself as a policy workspace with tailored policy news, legislation tracking and directories for professionals.

accessibility.note: Politico offers substantial free site/newsletter access, while deeper professional policy intelligence sits behind Pro subscriptions.

products.name: The 19th
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom focused on gender, politics, policy and power, useful for readers who want coverage of undercovered civic effects.

independence.note: The 19th describes itself as an independent nonprofit newsroom reporting on gender, politics, policy and power.

transparency.note: Its gift-acceptance policy explains donor limits, editorial independence and funding boundaries.

nonprofit.note: The 19th identifies as a nonprofit newsroom and solicits tax-deductible reader and philanthropic support.

depth.note: Its beat focuses on the policy and power implications of gender, race and politics rather than general breaking-news volume.

accessibility.note: The 19th publishes its journalism freely online and supports distribution through newsletters and syndication.

products.name: Grist
products.description: A nonprofit climate newsroom built around solutions, accountability and justice coverage, with free access and broad republishing.

independence.note: Grist describes itself as a nonprofit, independent media organization dedicated to climate journalism.

transparency.note: Grist publishes funding partners, Form 990 access and sponsorship context from its about page.

nonprofit.note: Grist says it is a nonprofit outlet and keeps its journalism outside a paywall.

depth.note: Grist reports daily, feature, investigation and visual stories on climate impacts, accountability and solutions.

accessibility.note: Grist says its journalism is never behind a paywall and is available for free republishing by partners.

products.name: Reveal
products.description: A nonprofit investigative outlet and public-radio/podcast operation from the Center for Investigative Reporting.

independence.note: The Center for Investigative Reporting, also known as Reveal, is described as a nonprofit newsroom focused on in-depth investigations.

transparency.note: Reveal's nonprofit structure and major grants are visible through philanthropic and public-radio partner disclosures, though its site-level standards pages are less prominent.

nonprofit.note: CIR/Reveal is a nonprofit investigative journalism organization supported by members and foundations.

depth.note: Reveal specializes in public-interest investigations on accountability, inequality and sustainability, often through podcast, radio and partner distribution.

accessibility.note: Reveal distributes investigative work through its website, public-radio show, podcast and media partners, though some formats are not a simple daily news feed.

products.name: The Trace
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom dedicated to gun-violence reporting, strongest for deep data, policy and accountability coverage.

independence.note: The Trace says it maintains a firewall between news coverage decisions and all revenue sources.

transparency.note: The Trace publishes donor and financial transparency policies, donor thresholds and Form 990 context.

nonprofit.note: The Trace identifies as a nonprofit 501(c)(3) corporation dedicated to gun-violence journalism.

depth.note: The Trace describes itself as the only newsroom exclusively dedicated to reporting on the U.S. gun violence crisis.

accessibility.note: The Trace keeps its gun-violence reporting free and offers newsletters, data hubs and local reporting projects.

products.name: Chalkbeat
products.description: A nonprofit education newsroom with local bureaus, strong ethics pages and a clear focus on school policy and practice.

independence.note: Chalkbeat says it is fiercely independent and does not take a position on the best path for education equity.

transparency.note: Chalkbeat publishes a detailed code of ethics, corrections practices and funding-model disclosure.

nonprofit.note: Chalkbeat identifies as a nonprofit news organization and Civic News Company newsroom.

depth.note: Chalkbeat's mission is deep local coverage of education policy and practice in multiple communities.

accessibility.note: Chalkbeat publishes free local and national education coverage, newsletters and republishing options.

products.name: States Newsroom
products.description: A nonprofit network focused on state politics and policy, useful for filling statehouse gaps left by shrinking local newsrooms.

independence.note: States Newsroom says its philanthropic model focuses on coverage of state politics and policy through independent nonprofit partners.

transparency.note: States Newsroom publishes an ethics policy that points reporters to SPJ and NPPA standards.

nonprofit.note: States Newsroom identifies as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit supported by readers and philanthropists.

depth.note: Its core depth signal is daily statehouse reporting and policy coverage across state capitals rather than national investigative projects.

accessibility.note: States Newsroom makes statehouse coverage free to read and widely republishable through News From The States and partner sites.

products.name: NOTUS
products.description: A nonprofit Washington newsroom from the Allbritton Journalism Institute, combining veteran editors with early-career reporters.

independence.note: NOTUS says its news judgments are made independently and not influenced by donors or revenue sources.

transparency.note: NOTUS says it will publish all revenue sources and donors giving $5,000 or more per year.

nonprofit.note: NOTUS describes itself as a nonpartisan news nonprofit under the 501(c)(3) Allbritton Journalism Institute.

depth.note: NOTUS covers government and politics from Washington with veteran reporters, editors and journalism fellows.

accessibility.note: NOTUS publishes politics and policy coverage online for free, with newsletters and local-news partnerships.

products.name: 404 Media
products.description: A journalist-owned technology newsroom focused on hidden internet, AI, privacy, cybersecurity and platform accountability stories.

independence.note: 404 Media says it is created, owned, written and edited by its founding journalists.

transparency.note: 404 Media explains its reader-supported business model and paywall approach in its launch note.

nonprofit.note: 404 Media is an independent commercial media company, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Its stated focus is beat reporting, investigations and scoops on hacking, cybersecurity, AI, privacy, surveillance and online communities.

accessibility.note: 404 Media publishes some stories and a newsletter freely, while full access is membership-based.

products.name: Consumer Reports
products.description: A nonprofit consumer-testing and advice organization, useful for electronics, privacy, safety and product-accountability decisions, with many ratings behind membership.

independence.note: Consumer Reports describes itself as an independent nonprofit member organization.

transparency.note: Consumer Reports publishes pages describing its research, testing and review work.

nonprofit.note: Consumer Reports identifies itself as a nonprofit member organization.

depth.note: Its public materials emphasize product testing, research, advice and marketplace accountability across consumer categories.

accessibility.note: Consumer Reports publishes some free advice, but many ratings and detailed reviews require membership or subscription access.

products.name: WIRED
products.description: A Conde Nast technology magazine with strong reporting on tech, business, culture and science, but ordinary commercial ownership and subscription friction.

independence.note: WIRED is part of Conde Nast, so it has commercial ownership rather than reader, nonprofit or public-media structure.

transparency.note: WIRED publishes an about and FAQ page, and Conde Nast publishes brand and editorial-standard information.

nonprofit.note: WIRED is a Conde Nast commercial media brand, not a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: WIRED describes its work as rigorous reporting and investigations on how technology affects business, politics, culture and science.

accessibility.note: WIRED offers some free journalism, but regular access is shaped by its subscription and membership model.

products.name: The Verge
products.description: A mainstream tech and culture newsroom with unusually explicit ethics rules, strong consumer-tech coverage and a mix of free and subscriber-supported access.

independence.note: The Verge is part of Vox Media, a commercial media company, while publishing ethics rules intended to protect editorial independence.

transparency.note: The Verge publishes an about page and a detailed ethics statement covering editorial standards and conflicts.

nonprofit.note: The Verge is a Vox Media commercial publication, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Its about page describes breaking news, reviews, features, investigations, video and podcasts about technology and culture.

accessibility.note: The Verge remains broadly accessible for many stories while also operating subscriber-supported products and access layers.

products.name: Ars Technica
products.description: A technically deep technology newsroom covering IT, cybersecurity, AI, science, space, operating systems and policy under Conde Nast ownership.

independence.note: Ars Technica is a Conde Nast publication, so it has commercial ownership rather than nonprofit or reader-owned structure.

transparency.note: Ars Technica publishes an about page and editorial ethos explaining its technical audience and standards.

nonprofit.note: Ars Technica is a Conde Nast commercial media brand, not a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: Ars covers IT, AI, science, cybersecurity, tech policy, computers, operating systems and related technical beats.

accessibility.note: Ars publishes substantial free coverage while also offering subscriptions and ad-light or member-supported access.

products.name: Tech Policy Press
products.description: A nonprofit newsroom and community venture focused on technology, democracy, platform power, privacy, surveillance, geopolitics and election integrity.

independence.note: Tech Policy Press says it retains full authority over editorial content and makes independent editorial judgments.

transparency.note: Its about page lists mission, funding years, donors and editorial-authority language.

nonprofit.note: Tech Policy Press describes itself as a nonprofit media and community venture and a 501(c)(3) organization.

depth.note: The outlet focuses on technology and democracy, platform power, ethics, geopolitics, oppression, privacy and election integrity.

accessibility.note: Tech Policy Press publishes its reporting, analysis and opinion work freely and solicits donations rather than relying on a hard subscription gate.

products.name: Engadget
products.description: A free mainstream consumer-technology news and reviews site, useful for device/platform coverage but less structurally independent than nonprofit or reader-owned sources.

independence.note: Engadget says companies cannot pay for coverage and its advertising arm and parent company are not involved in editorial decisions.

transparency.note: Engadget publishes about, FAQ and review-guideline pages explaining its editorial and review practices.

nonprofit.note: Engadget is a commercial consumer-technology publication, not a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: Engadget covers consumer technology news, reviews and global technology reporting with an emphasis on devices and platforms.

accessibility.note: Engadget is broadly free to read, with commercial advertising rather than a primary hard-paywall model.

products.name: STAT News
products.description: A commercial health, medicine and biotech newsroom with strong subject-matter depth and a significant subscriber layer.

independence.note: STAT says it was launched by John Henry, owner of The Boston Globe, and is part of Boston Globe Media.

transparency.note: STAT publishes ethics, AI policy and supporter links alongside its about and subscription information.

nonprofit.note: STAT is part of Boston Globe Media and is not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: STAT's about page emphasizes award-winning health, medicine, life-science, policy and investigative reporting.

accessibility.note: STAT publishes some free coverage and newsletters, but many deep products and unlimited access are tied to STAT+ subscriptions.

products.name: The Atlantic
products.description: A long-running magazine and digital publisher with strong analysis and essay depth, but commercial ownership and a subscription gate.

independence.note: The Atlantic announced Emerson Collective's majority ownership in 2017, replacing purely founder/operator ownership with philanthropist-investor ownership.

transparency.note: The Atlantic publishes terms and subscription access rules, but public editorial-standards disclosure is less visible than nonprofit peers.

nonprofit.note: The Atlantic is a commercial magazine and publisher, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: The Atlantic describes its work as politics, arts, letters and reporting on culture, science, national security, technology and literature.

accessibility.note: The Atlantic lets readers access a limited number of articles for free, with additional access requiring subscription.

products.name: NBC News
products.description: A major U.S. broadcast and digital news organization with very high reach, corporate ownership and visible but broad standards infrastructure.

independence.note: NBC News is part of NBCUniversal News Group within NBCUniversal, a large commercial media and entertainment company.

transparency.note: NBCU Academy describes the NBC News Group standards function and its role in accuracy, fairness and sensitive-story guidance.

nonprofit.note: NBC News is a commercial NBCUniversal brand, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: NBC News has national digital, broadcast, streaming, local and program brands, but its structure is broad mainstream news rather than nonprofit investigative specialization.

accessibility.note: NBCNews.com and NBC News NOW provide broad free digital and streaming access, while full broadcast/cable access can depend on distribution.

products.name: CBS News
products.description: A major U.S. broadcast, streaming and digital news organization with deep legacy programs and corporate Paramount ownership.

independence.note: CBS News is a Paramount brand, so large commercial entertainment-media ownership is the main independence context.

transparency.note: CBS News publishes principles for corrections, sourcing, anonymous sources, AI, opinion labeling and standards handling.

nonprofit.note: CBS News is a commercial Paramount brand, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: Paramount describes CBS News and Stations as a large news division with major broadcast, streaming, radio, podcast and digital properties.

accessibility.note: CBS News provides CBSNews.com and a free 24/7 streaming news network alongside broadcast distribution.

products.name: AP Fact Check
products.description: A fact-checking desk from the Associated Press that debunks viral claims and explains evidence in AP style.

independence.note: AP's news-values page emphasizes independence, impartiality, accuracy and freedom from bias for AP journalism.

transparency.note: AP Fact Check labels claims, assessments and factual explanation in a public archive of misinformation debunks.

nonprofit.note: AP is a not-for-profit news cooperative, but not a donor-funded civic nonprofit like many investigative outlets.

depth.note: AP fact checkers combat misinformation by debunking false and misleading claims, usually in concise article form.

accessibility.note: The AP Fact Check archive is publicly readable online without a reader subscription.

products.name: Reuters Fact Check
products.description: A Reuters verification and fact-checking feed for debunking misinformation tied to news events and online claims.

independence.note: Reuters Trust Principles require integrity, independence and freedom from bias in Reuters news operations.

transparency.note: Reuters publishes standards covering accuracy, correction, balance, sourcing and conflicts.

nonprofit.note: Reuters is part of Thomson Reuters, a commercial information company, so it scores low on nonprofit/public ownership.

depth.note: Reuters Agency describes a specialist fact-checking team covering topics and regions, with a misinformation verification feed.

accessibility.note: Many Reuters fact-check articles are publicly readable, while some Reuters products and feeds are aimed at paying media clients.

products.name: USAFacts
products.description: A nonpartisan civic data project that turns U.S. government data into public explainers, charts and topic pages.

independence.note: USAFacts describes itself as a not-for-profit, nonpartisan civic initiative with no political agenda.

transparency.note: USAFacts says it relies on government data and publishes methodology and source context for its data work.

nonprofit.note: USAFacts identifies as a not-for-profit civic initiative making government data easier to access and understand.

depth.note: USAFacts organizes government data across crime, defense, economy, education, health, population and other policy areas.

accessibility.note: USAFacts publishes free public topic pages, charts and newsletters using plain-language data presentation.

products.name: OpenSecrets
products.description: A U.S. campaign-finance and lobbying data watchdog that helps readers trace political money and influence.

independence.note: OpenSecrets frames its mission around nonpartisan tracking of money in U.S. politics and public accountability.

transparency.note: OpenSecrets publishes campaign-finance, lobbying, outside-spending and personal-finance databases with sourceable records.

nonprofit.note: OpenSecrets is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit formed from campaign-finance transparency organizations.

depth.note: OpenSecrets tracks federal and state campaign finance, lobbying, revolving-door and outside-spending data.

accessibility.note: Core searches and profiles are public, while deeper professional tooling and bulk products may require paid access.

products.name: Ballotpedia
products.description: A nonprofit encyclopedia of U.S. elections, candidates, ballot measures, courts, offices and policy topics.

independence.note: Ballotpedia says it provides accurate and objective information on elections, politics and policy.

transparency.note: Ballotpedia publishes editorial and correction pages explaining its encyclopedia model and standards.

nonprofit.note: Ballotpedia is operated by the Lucy Burns Institute, a nonprofit organization.

depth.note: Ballotpedia covers federal, state and local politics, elections, candidates, ballot measures, courts and policy.

accessibility.note: Ballotpedia pages are free to read and searchable as a public web encyclopedia.

products.name: Congress.gov
products.description: The official U.S. federal legislative information site for bills, resolutions, laws, members, committees and congressional records.

independence.note: Congress.gov is an official primary-record source rather than independent journalism, so it is authoritative but not editorially independent from government.

transparency.note: The Law Library of Congress describes Congress.gov as the official website for accurate, timely and complete U.S. federal legislative information.

nonprofit.note: Congress.gov is presented by the Library of Congress using public congressional and government data sources.

depth.note: Congress.gov provides bills, resolutions, summaries, status, public laws, roll-call votes and legislative resources.

accessibility.note: The site is free to search and browse, though legislative status and bill text still require civic literacy to interpret.

products.name: Federal Register
products.description: The official daily journal of the U.S. government for rules, proposed rules, public notices and presidential documents.

independence.note: The Federal Register is an official government publication, so it is a primary record rather than an independent interpretive source.

transparency.note: The National Archives describes the Federal Register as the official journal providing legal notice of rules, notices and presidential documents.

nonprofit.note: The Federal Register is published through the Office of the Federal Register within the National Archives and Records Administration.

depth.note: FederalRegister.gov includes rules, proposed rules, notices, public-inspection documents and reader aids for federal rulemaking.

accessibility.note: FederalRegister.gov is publicly searchable and provides reader aids, though legal notices can still be dense.

products.name: CourtListener
products.description: A nonprofit legal-search and alert platform for court opinions, federal filings, judges and legal research data.

independence.note: CourtListener is created by Free Law Project, a nonprofit focused on public access to legal information rather than commercial legal publishing.

transparency.note: Free Law Project explains CourtListener as a searchable archive of court data, opinions, oral arguments, judges and federal filings.

nonprofit.note: Free Law Project identifies as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

depth.note: CourtListener contains millions of legal opinions from federal and state courts plus alerts and raw data for deeper analysis.

accessibility.note: CourtListener offers free legal search for lawyers, journalists, academics and the public.

products.name: MuckRock
products.description: A nonprofit public-records platform and newsroom for filing, tracking, publishing and reporting from FOIA requests.

independence.note: MuckRock says it brings journalists, researchers and the public together to request, analyze and share government information.

transparency.note: MuckRock publishes requests, documents and project pages that let readers inspect public-records trails.

nonprofit.note: MuckRock Foundation identifies as a nonprofit collaborative news site and 501(c)(3) organization.

depth.note: MuckRock supports public-records requests, document analysis and collaborative reporting projects, with depth depending on the request or investigation.

accessibility.note: Published requests and documents are public, while filing requests through the platform can involve fees or account workflow.

products.name: USAspending.gov
products.description: The official U.S. federal spending data portal for contracts, grants, loans and other federal awards.

independence.note: USAspending.gov is an official government data source, so it is primary evidence rather than independent civic analysis.

transparency.note: USAspending describes itself as the official open data source of federal spending information, including contracts, grants and loans.

nonprofit.note: USAspending.gov is a public federal-government data portal rather than a commercial publisher.

depth.note: The site provides searchable award, agency, recipient, spending-explorer and downloadable spending data.

accessibility.note: The portal is public and searchable, though interpreting award data and accounting categories takes some data literacy.

products.name: FEC Campaign Finance Data
products.description: The official U.S. federal campaign-finance data portal for candidates, committees, receipts, spending and filings.

independence.note: FEC data is official regulatory data, authoritative for filings but not independent journalism or watchdog analysis.

transparency.note: The FEC data portal lets users see how candidates and committees raise and spend money in federal elections.

nonprofit.note: The Federal Election Commission is a public federal agency rather than a commercial media source.

depth.note: The portal includes candidate, committee, contribution, spending and filing records for federal campaigns.

accessibility.note: FEC campaign-finance data is public and searchable, but legal categories and filing mechanics can be hard for casual users.

products.name: LegiScan
products.description: A nonpartisan legislative-tracking service that covers Congress and all 50 state legislatures, with free public tracking plus paid data tiers.

independence.note: LegiScan describes itself as an impartial and nonpartisan legislative tracking, reporting and data service.

transparency.note: The site publishes bill, schedule, report, API and dataset information, but it is not an official legislative source itself.

nonprofit.note: LegiScan identifies as LegiScan LLC, so it scores low on nonprofit/public ownership despite free public access.

depth.note: LegiScan tracks legislation across Congress, 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico, with bill reports and public API options.

accessibility.note: LegiScan offers free public accounts and searches, while heavier national tracking and API use move into paid tiers.

products.name: VOTE411
products.brand: League of Women Voters Education Fund
products.description: A nonpartisan U.S. election-information tool for registration checks, polling places, ballot information and candidate research.

independence.note: The League of Women Voters describes VOTE411 as a virtual, nonpartisan election-information resource.

transparency.note: VOTE411 lists the kinds of election information it provides, including registration, candidate data, ballot measures and polling-place details.

nonprofit.note: VOTE411 is brought to the public by the League of Women Voters Education Fund.

depth.note: The League says VOTE411 provides bilingual election information in all 50 states and DC, updated as information changes.

accessibility.note: VOTE411 is a free web resource for checking registration, finding polling places, learning about candidates and viewing ballot information.

products.name: Vote Smart
products.description: A nonprofit U.S. candidate and elected-official research service covering officials, votes, issues and voter tools.

independence.note: Vote Smart says it provides free, factual, unbiased information and is staffed by people unaffiliated with any party.

transparency.note: Vote Smart presents offices, officials, legislation and issues as separate voter-research categories rather than opaque ratings alone.

nonprofit.note: Vote Smart says that as a nonprofit it is not backed by big money or special interests.

depth.note: Vote Smart says it has information on more than 220,000 candidates and covers lawmaker votes, offices and issue information.

accessibility.note: Vote Smart says it shares millions of facts for free to all Americans.

products.name: DocumentCloud
products.description: An open-source document platform used by newsrooms to publish, annotate, search and analyze primary-source documents.

independence.note: DocumentCloud is part of the MuckRock Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit focused on trust and transparency.

transparency.note: DocumentCloud exists to help journalists share, analyze, annotate and publish source documents to the open web.

nonprofit.note: The DocumentCloud about page identifies it as part of MuckRock Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

depth.note: DocumentCloud describes itself as an all-in-one platform for organizing, analyzing, annotating, searching and embedding primary-source documents.

accessibility.note: DocumentCloud helps publish documents to the open web, though upload and newsroom workflows require an account and tool literacy.

products.name: LittleSis
products.description: A nonprofit public-interest research platform for mapping relationships among influential people and organizations.

independence.note: LittleSis describes the Public Accountability Initiative as a nonprofit public-interest research organization focused on corporate and government accountability.

transparency.note: LittleSis describes itself as a free, open-source research platform and database of who-knows-who in business and government.

nonprofit.note: The LittleSis about page identifies the Public Accountability Initiative, known as LittleSis, as a nonprofit public-interest research organization.

depth.note: LittleSis focuses on power research into social, political and economic relationships that shape policy and accountability.

accessibility.note: LittleSis says its power research database is free and open source, while serious use still requires research skill and context checking.

products.name: OpenCorporates
products.description: A legal-entity data service that helps researchers, journalists and public-interest groups trace company records across jurisdictions.

independence.note: OpenCorporates frames its mission around corporate transparency and improved access to foundational legal-entity data.

transparency.note: OpenCorporates says it provides company records from more than 140 government registries and official sources worldwide.

nonprofit.note: OpenCorporates offers enterprise bulk-data and API products, so it is scored below nonprofit/public-data providers despite its public-benefit mission.

depth.note: OpenCorporates says it offers the world's largest open legal-entity database with a unified set of company records.

accessibility.note: OpenCorporates supports free at-scale access for journalists, NGOs, universities and anti-crime research groups, while commercial use can require paid access.

products.name: Open States
products.description: A state-legislation data and API project, now under Plural/SAI360, with free bill search plus bulk and API access.

independence.note: Open States now sits under Plural/SAI360 rather than an independent nonprofit civic-data home, which lowers independence for public-interest news use.

transparency.note: Open States says its data is available through bulk downloads and APIs, with API documentation and issue links public.

nonprofit.note: The project page says Open States is now Plural/SAI360, so it is scored as a commercial policy-data service rather than a nonprofit source.

depth.note: The API documentation covers state legislative information including jurisdictions, people and bill search methods.

accessibility.note: Open States says free bill search and legislator lookup remain available, while API use requires a registered key.

products.name: FactCheck.org
products.description: A nonprofit U.S. political and viral-claim fact-checker rooted in the Annenberg Public Policy Center.

independence.note: FactCheck.org says it is nonpartisan and does not accept funds from corporations, unions, partisan organizations or advocacy groups.

transparency.note: FactCheck.org publishes process and funding pages explaining selection, research, editing, corrections and financial disclosure.

nonprofit.note: FactCheck.org describes itself as a nonprofit project of the Annenberg Public Policy Center at the University of Pennsylvania.

depth.note: Its process page describes monitoring major U.S. political actors and publishing researched fact-check articles, including correction procedures.

accessibility.note: FactCheck.org articles, Ask FactCheck and issue archives are publicly available without a paywall.

products.name: PolitiFact
products.description: A U.S. political fact-checking outlet known for its Truth-O-Meter ratings and Poynter nonprofit ownership.

independence.note: PolitiFact says rating and coverage decisions are made by independent journalists, while noting platform partnerships and commercial services.

transparency.note: PolitiFact publishes a detailed methodology covering ownership, funding, sourcing, ratings, corrections and IFCN participation.

nonprofit.note: PolitiFact says it is owned by the nonprofit Poynter Institute and functions as a not-for-profit national news organization.

depth.note: Its methodology emphasizes independence, fairness, thorough reporting, clear writing and on-the-record sourcing for claim checks.

accessibility.note: PolitiFact publishes its fact checks and Truth-O-Meter archives for free online.

products.name: Full Fact
products.description: A UK charity that fact-checks public debate, viral content and institutions while publishing source trails and correction pressure.

independence.note: Full Fact says it is independent and has fundraising guidelines, neutrality safeguards and cross-viewpoint governance.

transparency.note: Full Fact publishes how it chooses claims, gathers evidence, uses sources, reviews work and follows up after fact checks.

nonprofit.note: Full Fact is a registered charity and non-profit company limited by guarantee in England and Wales.

depth.note: Full Fact covers fact checks, investigations, in-depth analysis, government tracking, training and policy work around misinformation.

accessibility.note: Full Fact says its fact checks are free to read, though they rely on donations and funders to produce.

products.name: Snopes
products.description: A long-running internet rumor and misinformation reference, useful for viral claims but commercially owned rather than nonprofit.

independence.note: Snopes describes itself as an independent publication, but its disclosures identify corporate ownership under Snopes Media Group.

transparency.note: Snopes publishes about, disclosure, rating and FAQ pages explaining its ownership, process and rating labels.

nonprofit.note: Snopes disclosures describe corporate ownership, so it scores low on the nonprofit/public criterion.

depth.note: Snopes maintains a large archive of fact checks on urban legends, folklore, myths, rumors and misinformation.

accessibility.note: Snopes fact checks and archives are broadly readable online, though the site uses commercial web and membership mechanics.

products.name: Bellingcat
products.description: An open-source investigative collective that publishes verifiable methods for digital investigation and accountability reporting.

independence.note: Bellingcat describes itself as independent and publishes editorial standards, but funding includes foundations, workshops and in-kind company support.

transparency.note: Bellingcat publishes editorial standards covering evidence, transparency, corrections, anonymous sources, conflicts and generative AI.

nonprofit.note: Bellingcat says it is composed of a charitable foundation in the Netherlands and a US 501(c)(3).

depth.note: Bellingcat specializes in open-source and social-media investigations, with methods and evidence presented for public verification.

accessibility.note: Bellingcat publishes investigations and resources freely online; paid workshops are separate from the core article archive.

products.name: AFP Fact Check
products.description: A global multilingual fact-checking desk inside AFP, useful for viral visual claims and international misinformation.

independence.note: AFP says its founding statute protects its voice from political, commercial or ideological influence, but AFP Fact Check sits inside a large news agency.

transparency.note: AFP Fact Check publishes how it works, editorial standards and a corrections page for fact-check updates.

nonprofit.note: AFP Fact Check is a department of Agence France-Presse rather than a nonprofit or public-media charity.

depth.note: AFP Fact Check runs multilingual regional desks and prioritizes harmful misinformation including health, democracy and hate-speech claims.

accessibility.note: AFP Fact Check publishes a free public website with topical and regional fact-check archives.

products.name: Lead Stories
products.description: A fast viral-misinformation fact-checker that monitors trending posts, including AI-generated images and videos.

independence.note: Lead Stories says Meta, ByteDance and Google have no say over its fact-check choices or conclusions, but those platform/client relationships shape its context.

transparency.note: Lead Stories publishes about, how-we-work, corrections, funding and IFCN/EFCSN verification links.

nonprofit.note: Lead Stories identifies itself as Lead Stories LLC, a Colorado company, so it scores low on nonprofit/public structure.

depth.note: Lead Stories focuses on fast debunking of trending false, misleading, deceptive or inaccurate stories, videos and images.

accessibility.note: Lead Stories publishes public fact checks and archives online without a reader paywall.

products.name: Ad Fontes Media
products.description: A source-rating and media-bias chart company that scores outlets for reliability and political bias using analyst panels.

independence.note: Ad Fontes says it is a Colorado public benefit corporation and for-profit business with a public mission to rate news.

transparency.note: Ad Fontes publishes a detailed methodology explaining reliability and bias ratings, analyst panels and content-analysis process.

nonprofit.note: Ad Fontes is explicit that public benefit corporation status still means a for-profit business, so it scores below nonprofit/public outlets.

depth.note: Ad Fontes rates news and news-like sources for bias and reliability and provides an interactive media-bias chart and data platform.

accessibility.note: Ad Fontes provides public chart access and educational material, while deeper data-platform access is a paid product.

products.name: NewsGuard
products.description: A commercial news-reliability ratings and browser-extension service that uses journalist-written site labels and criteria.

independence.note: NewsGuard says it accepts no fees from rated websites, but its revenue comes from licensing ratings and reader subscriptions.

transparency.note: NewsGuard publishes its rating process and nine journalistic criteria for reliability and transparency assessments.

nonprofit.note: NewsGuard Technologies is a commercial company, not a nonprofit or public-media organization.

depth.note: NewsGuard deploys journalists and editors to produce reliability ratings and detailed labels for news and information websites.

accessibility.note: NewsGuard offers a free trial, then charges a monthly subscription for continued consumer browser-extension access.

products.name: Media Bias/Fact Check
products.description: A large free media-bias and factuality database that is useful for lateral reading, but more subjective than formal newsroom standards.

independence.note: MBFC says funding comes from reader donations, advertising and memberships rather than corporations, foundations or advocacy groups.
