transparency.note: MBFC publishes a methodology for weighted ideological-bias and factual-reliability ratings, but the approach remains partly subjective.

nonprofit.note: MBFC's own funding page describes reader donations, advertising and subscriptions, not nonprofit or public-media status.

depth.note: MBFC says its database includes 10,000+ media sources, journalists, politicians and countries.

accessibility.note: The core source-search and rating pages are free to access, supported by ads, donations and membership options.

products.name: The Trust Project
products.description: A nonprofit standards effort that helps newsrooms disclose ownership, ethics, labels, sourcing, methods and corrections to readers.

independence.note: The Trust Project says its policies and Trust Indicators are shaped and enforced independently from funding sources.

transparency.note: The Trust Project publishes Trust Indicators for labels, journalist expertise, citations, methods, local sourcing, diversity and feedback.

nonprofit.note: The Trust Project says it is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

depth.note: The project is a standards and newsroom-transparency framework, not a daily newsroom or rating database.

accessibility.note: Trust Indicators and public explainers are freely available online for readers and news organizations.

products.name: IFCN Code of Principles
products.description: A global standards reference for evaluating fact-checkers on nonpartisanship, sources, funding, methodology and corrections.

independence.note: IFCN is a Poynter unit that connects fact-checkers worldwide and promotes nonpartisan, transparent fact-checking.

transparency.note: The Code of Principles lays out commitments for nonpartisanship, source transparency, funding transparency, methodology and corrections.

nonprofit.note: IFCN is housed at the nonprofit Poynter Institute, not a commercial news-rating company.

depth.note: The code is a standards framework for fact-checking organizations, useful for evaluation but not a reporting archive.

accessibility.note: The code, commitments and signatory information are public online resources.

products.name: RumorGuard
products.description: A News Literacy Project resource that turns viral misinformation examples into short debunks and teachable verification habits.

independence.note: The News Literacy Project describes itself as a nonpartisan education nonprofit focused on news-literacy instruction.

transparency.note: RumorGuard explains viral rumors through quick looks, takeaways, five credibility factors and links to related resources.

nonprofit.note: RumorGuard is created by the News Literacy Project, a nonpartisan education nonprofit.

depth.note: RumorGuard is strongest as short-form viral-rumor teaching and practice, not as a deep investigative newsroom.

accessibility.note: RumorGuard pages and News Literacy Project resources are freely available online.

products.name: Techdirt
products.description: An independent tech-policy and internet-culture publication useful for copyright, platform, moderation, innovation and digital-rights context.

independence.note: Techdirt describes its effort to stand as an independent publication supported directly by readers.

transparency.note: Techdirt publishes its company/about material and explains reader-support and funding context, though it is less formal than a nonprofit annual report.

nonprofit.note: Techdirt is an independent commercial publication rather than a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Its public archive focuses on tech policy, copyright, platform governance, privacy and innovation debates with frequent analysis.

accessibility.note: Techdirt publishes articles freely online and asks readers to support the publication directly.

products.name: KrebsOnSecurity
products.description: An independent cybersecurity reporting site centered on cybercrime, breaches, fraud infrastructure and security-industry accountability.

independence.note: Brian Krebs' about page identifies the site around his post-Washington Post independent security reporting work.

transparency.note: The about page provides author background and reporting history, but the site has less institutional funding disclosure than nonprofit newsrooms.

nonprofit.note: KrebsOnSecurity is an independent journalist site, not a nonprofit or public-media institution.

depth.note: Krebs' background includes extensive security and cybercrime reporting, and the site publishes detailed investigations on breaches, fraud and infrastructure abuse.

accessibility.note: KrebsOnSecurity publishes its reporting freely online.

products.name: Platformer
products.description: A journalist-led technology publication focused on platforms, social media, AI, labor and governance inside major tech companies.

independence.note: Platformer's about page identifies it as written by Casey Newton and Zoe Schiffer, with background on their prior reporting careers.

transparency.note: The about page explains authorship, publishing cadence and subscription model, though not the kind of annual-report disclosure used by nonprofits.

nonprofit.note: Platformer is an independent subscription publication rather than a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: Platformer's stated beat is the intersection of Silicon Valley and democracy, with regular platform and technology reporting.

accessibility.note: Platformer publishes some free posts, but much of the newsletter is subscription-supported.

products.name: MIT Technology Review
products.description: A long-running technology publication for understanding emerging technologies, AI, climate tech and digital systems in broader context.

independence.note: MIT Technology Review says its coverage is editorially independent, including from its MIT ownership.

transparency.note: Its media-kit material discloses advertising, brand partnerships, sponsored content, research and event products alongside journalism.

nonprofit.note: MIT Technology Review derives authority from MIT ownership, but operates as a global media company with subscriptions, events and commercial partnerships.

depth.note: The publication describes authoritative journalism, news analysis, business reports, features, reviews and interactive digital experiences on technology impacts.

accessibility.note: MIT Technology Review mixes free newsletters/articles with subscriptions, premium reports and paid event/research offerings.

products.name: Columbia Journalism Review
products.description: A journalism-review publication that monitors press performance, media ethics, news business models and the public role of journalism.

independence.note: CJR describes itself as an independent nonprofit positioned to help journalism be at its best.

transparency.note: CJR publishes about, masthead, contact, membership and support pages for its journalism-review work.

nonprofit.note: CJR's membership page identifies it as an independent nonprofit.

depth.note: CJR's stated role is a voice of journalism, with rigorous analysis of how news is produced and understood.

accessibility.note: CJR publishes much of its media criticism and analysis freely online while asking for membership support.

products.name: Nieman Lab
products.description: A Harvard/Nieman publication covering how journalism, platforms, audiences, AI and business models are changing.

independence.note: Nieman Lab is part of the Nieman Foundation at Harvard and frames its mission around helping journalism adapt in the internet age.

transparency.note: Its about page lists team members, foundation context, copyright/licensing and republishing terms.

nonprofit.note: Nieman Lab is published by the Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard rather than a commercial media company.

depth.note: The about page describes daily reporting on significant developments in journalism and digital media for an international audience.

accessibility.note: Nieman Lab says its content is generally available under a Creative Commons noncommercial share-alike license.

products.name: Global Investigative Journalism Network
products.description: A global nonprofit network that supports investigative and data journalism with resources, training, conferences and cross-border knowledge sharing.

independence.note: GIJN describes itself as a global network supporting investigative journalism, with membership limited to nonprofit, NGO and educational organizations or equivalents.

transparency.note: GIJN publishes about, membership and network pages explaining its structure and member eligibility.

nonprofit.note: GIJN membership is open to nonprofit, NGO and educational organizations that support investigative reporting and data journalism.

depth.note: GIJN functions mainly as a support network and resource hub for investigative journalists rather than a single daily newsroom.

accessibility.note: GIJN publishes resources, guides and journalism-support material freely online.

products.name: Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project
products.description: A mission-driven investigative newsroom and network focused on organized crime, corruption and cross-border accountability reporting.

independence.note: OCCRP says it is a mission-driven nonprofit newsroom partnering with other media outlets, while also publishing an FAQ on funding and editorial policies.

transparency.note: OCCRP publishes about-us and funding/editorial-policy FAQ material describing its structure, focus and funding questions.

nonprofit.note: OCCRP identifies as a mission-driven nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: OCCRP says it is one of the largest investigative journalism organizations in the world and focuses on stories that lead to real-world action.

accessibility.note: OCCRP publishes investigations freely online and through partner outlets.

products.name: Forbidden Stories
products.description: A nonprofit collaborative-journalism project that continues investigations by journalists who are threatened, jailed or killed.

independence.note: Forbidden Stories describes its nonprofit mission as protecting and continuing the work of threatened or silenced journalists.

transparency.note: Forbidden Stories publishes mission, donor, partner and investigation-collaboration material.

nonprofit.note: Forbidden Stories identifies itself as a nonprofit organization.

depth.note: The organization says each investigation gathers a consortium of journalists and media organizations to continue public-interest stories.

accessibility.note: Forbidden Stories emphasizes access to public-interest information and publishes investigations and partner work openly.

products.name: Lighthouse Reports
products.description: A Netherlands-based nonprofit investigative newsroom building collaborative investigations on migration, conflict, corruption, surveillance and public-interest systems.

independence.note: Lighthouse Reports says editorial independence is essential and that donors do not impose conditions restricting its journalism.

transparency.note: Its about page discloses nonprofit status, funding mix and public-benefit registration context.

nonprofit.note: Lighthouse Reports identifies as a nonprofit investigative newsroom based in the Netherlands.

depth.note: The newsroom describes complex transnational investigations that blend traditional investigative journalism with open-source and other emerging methods.

accessibility.note: Lighthouse works with media partners and publishes public-interest investigations and explainers online.

products.name: FRONTLINE
products.description: PBS's long-running investigative documentary program, strong for deep video reporting and public-interest explainers.

independence.note: FRONTLINE is part of PBS public media and is funded through viewers, CPB and foundation support rather than a commercial owner.

transparency.note: The PBS show page discloses funding context and connects FRONTLINE to PBS public-media standards and station support.

nonprofit.note: PBS identifies itself as a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization.

depth.note: PBS describes FRONTLINE as investigative journalism that questions, explains and changes the world.

accessibility.note: FRONTLINE is available to stream on PBS.org and the PBS app, though some extended access may depend on PBS Passport.

products.name: Lawfare
products.description: A nonprofit specialist publication for national security, courts, cybersecurity, executive power and foreign-policy law.

independence.note: Lawfare says it is a nonprofit multimedia publication providing nonpartisan analysis of legal and policy issues.

transparency.note: Lawfare publishes about, masthead and team pages, though it is more expert-analysis oriented than a broad transparent newsroom.

nonprofit.note: Lawfare identifies as a nonprofit publication published by the Lawfare Institute.

depth.note: Lawfare aims for academic-level depth with magazine-level readability across national security law and policy topics.

accessibility.note: Lawfare says all content is provided free of charge and without a subscription.

products.name: Just Security
products.description: A nonprofit daily law-and-policy journal focused on national security, democracy, rule of law and human rights.

independence.note: Just Security says it is editorially independent and nonpartisan.

transparency.note: Its about page identifies editorial scope, institutional home and donation route through NYU.

nonprofit.note: Just Security describes itself as a nonprofit daily digital law and policy journal housed at NYU School of Law's Reiss Center.

depth.note: Just Security publishes expert analysis and informational resources on national security, democracy, rights and rule-of-law issues.

accessibility.note: Just Security says it provides material without paywalls, subscriptions or ads.

products.name: Bolts
products.description: A nonprofit outlet covering overlooked local elections, prosecutors, sheriffs, courts, voting rights and democracy infrastructure.

independence.note: Bolts says it maintains a donor-editorial firewall and gives donors no right to review or influence articles.

transparency.note: Bolts publishes its structure, board, finances, donor disclosure policy, editorial-independence policy and corrections policy.

nonprofit.note: Bolts says it is operated by The Political Report, Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation.

depth.note: Bolts focuses on local institutions that shape criminal justice, policing, voting rights and democracy but are often overlooked.

accessibility.note: Bolts offers latest stories, RSS, newsletters and election-resource pages openly online.

products.name: Spotlight PA
products.description: A Pennsylvania nonprofit newsroom focused on state government, statewide issues, investigations and republication for local outlets.

independence.note: Spotlight PA describes itself as independent, nonpartisan and nonprofit, serving public interest rather than profit motives.

transparency.note: Spotlight PA publishes mission, team, board, partners, supporters, funding and impact pages.

nonprofit.note: Spotlight PA says it is an independent 501(c)(3) organization.

depth.note: The newsroom's mission is to hold powerful public and private forces accountable through investigative and public-service journalism.

accessibility.note: Spotlight PA says it does not charge for access and shares journalism with more than 100 Pennsylvania newsrooms at no cost.

products.name: Bridge Michigan
products.description: A Michigan nonprofit newsroom focused on nonpartisan public-policy, civic-life and watchdog reporting.

independence.note: The Center for Michigan says Bridge Michigan is committed to fact-based, nonpartisan journalism for public-policy and civic life.

transparency.note: Bridge Michigan publishes staff, funders, corrections, republication, ethics and conflict-of-interest links through its about navigation.

nonprofit.note: The Center for Michigan is incorporated as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and publishes Bridge Michigan.

depth.note: Bridge Michigan focuses on in-depth explanatory and watchdog reporting as traditional newspaper capacity declines.

accessibility.note: Bridge Michigan says it publishes nearly every day and is available free via web, email and social media.

products.name: Honolulu Civil Beat
products.description: A Hawaii nonprofit newsroom focused on investigative, watchdog and enterprise reporting for local civic life.

independence.note: Civil Beat is nonprofit and reader-supported, while also disclosing substantial Omidyar fund support as an influence context.

transparency.note: Civil Beat's about page discloses nonprofit status, funding sources, INN membership and its watchdog mission.

nonprofit.note: Honolulu Civil Beat says it is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt news organization.

depth.note: Civil Beat says it uses investigative and watchdog journalism plus in-depth enterprise reporting to inform Hawaii residents.

accessibility.note: Civil Beat removed its paywall in 2016 to expand access to local information.

products.name: Block Club Chicago
products.description: A nonprofit Chicago neighborhood newsroom focused on reliable local coverage across diverse communities.

independence.note: MacArthur describes Block Club Chicago as a nonprofit, reader-funded newsroom serving Chicago communities.

transparency.note: Block Club is identifiable as Block Club Chicago NFP and publishes a privacy policy/app presence, though funding transparency is less centralized than some peers.

nonprofit.note: The App Store lists the developer as Block Club Chicago NFP, and MacArthur describes the outlet as nonprofit.

depth.note: MacArthur says Block Club covers Chicago neighborhoods with accurate, nuanced and comprehensive local reporting.

accessibility.note: Block Club offers a free app and accessible coverage routes, but paid membership/premium story limits lower full accessibility.

products.name: Semafor
products.description: A global news startup built around visibly separated facts, reporter analysis, counter-narratives and global perspectives.

independence.note: Semafor describes itself as an independent news platform, while its 2026 expansion note also discloses financing and an events-led model.

transparency.note: Semafor says its Semaform structure separates facts, analysis, opinion, counter-narratives and global perspectives.

nonprofit.note: Semafor is a commercial news company, not a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: Semafor says it is expanding beat journalists in Washington, Wall Street, Silicon Valley, politics, global business, finance and economics.

accessibility.note: Semafor publishes web stories and free email briefings, making it more accessible than hard-paywalled specialist outlets.

products.name: Tangle
products.description: An independent politics newsletter that summarizes arguments from the right, left and center, then separates its own take.

independence.note: Tangle says Tangle Media LLC is owned by Isaac Saul and is independent, nonpartisan and subscriber-supported.

transparency.note: Tangle explains its format, including basic facts, views from left/right/center, its own take, staff dissent and corrections.

nonprofit.note: Tangle is an LLC and subscriber-supported media organization, not a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: Tangle says each newsletter is about a 10-minute read and aims to present nuance from multiple political perspectives.

accessibility.note: Tangle says Monday-through-Thursday editions are free for everyone, with Friday editions behind a paywall.

products.name: The Dispatch
products.description: A subscription-supported politics and culture outlet with fact-based reporting, analysis, newsletters, podcasts and a public corrections practice.

independence.note: The Dispatch describes itself as a digital media company built for fact-based reporting and commentary informed by conservative principles.

transparency.note: The Dispatch publishes a corrections policy and monthly correction roundups, making errors and standards visible.

nonprofit.note: The Dispatch is an independent commercial media company rather than a nonprofit or public-media outlet.

depth.note: The Dispatch covers politics, policy, culture, law, religion and related topics through reporting, newsletters, podcasts and explainers.

accessibility.note: The Dispatch uses a membership model with trials and paid tiers, so full access is less open than free or nonprofit newsrooms.

products.name: The Bulwark
products.description: A reader-supported politics and culture publication with newsletters, podcasts and analysis, especially visible in the anti-authoritarian media niche.

independence.note: The Bulwark says it is reader-supported and discloses ownership by Center Enterprises, Inc., operating as Bulwark Media.

transparency.note: Its about page explains mission, membership model, pricing, Substack platform use, ownership and advertising contact.

nonprofit.note: The Bulwark is owned by Center Enterprises, Inc. and is not a nonprofit newsroom.

depth.note: Bulwark+ membership includes articles, newsletters, podcasts, live events, community features and special projects.

accessibility.note: The Bulwark says democracy coverage should not be entirely behind a paywall, but full Bulwark+ access is paid.

products.name: The Information
products.description: A deeply reported subscription publication for technology and business news, strong on original scoops but intentionally less accessible.

independence.note: Founder Jessica Lessin says she owns the publication and that it has no venture-capital or corporate owners.

transparency.note: The about page discloses ownership, editorial leadership, teams, bureaus, business deals and contact routes.

nonprofit.note: The Information is an owner-operated commercial subscription publication, not a nonprofit outlet.

depth.note: The Information describes its work as deeply reported technology-industry articles that readers will not find elsewhere.

accessibility.note: The publication is subscriber-oriented, with premium newsletters, data tools and group subscriptions lowering open public access.
